title: Feet Like a Deer’s
old_p1: Habakkuk was a prophet long ago, a man who speaks for Heavenly Father. Hard times were coming to his land.
Habakkuk sang a prayer. He said that even if the fig trees did not bloom, and no grapes grew, and the sheep were gone…
“Yet I will rejoice in the Lord,” Habakkuk said. Rejoice means to be very glad. Even in hard times, he would be glad in the Lord.
old_p2: He sang, “The Lord is my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds’ feet.” A hind is a deer. Deer climb steep, rocky hills and do not fall. The Lord would help Habakkuk walk strong in hard, high places.
When something feels hard, the Lord can make you strong. Tonight, wiggle your feet, then let them rest. He will help you climb.
p1: Habakkuk told the people what Heavenly Father said. He knew hard times were coming to his land.
So Habakkuk sang a prayer. Maybe the fig trees would not bloom. Maybe no grapes would grow, and the sheep would be gone.
“Yet I will rejoice in the Lord,” Habakkuk sang. Even with empty fields, he would still be glad in the Lord.
p2: He sang, “The Lord is my strength.” He said the Lord would make his feet like a deer’s feet. Deer climb steep, rocky hills and do not slip. The Lord would help Habakkuk walk strong in hard, high places.
When something feels hard, the Lord can make you strong too. Tonight, wiggle your feet, then let them rest. He will help you climb.
